title: K-injective derived direct-image comparisons for subterminal slices
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ subterminal objects; no covering hypothesis is imposed. Put $W=U\times V$. Use the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $\mathcal E$ and its localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $j_Z^*$ for restriction to $Z=U,V,W$ and $k_U^*,k_V^*$ for restriction to $W$ within the $U,V$ slices. All these module categories admit K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Restriction and its underived right adjoint preserve K-injective complexes. On module sheaves this right adjoint is
$$(j_{Z*}F)(C)=F(C\times Z\to Z),$$
with $R(C)$ acting by restriction to $R(C\times Z)$; $k_{U*},k_{V*}$ have the same formula inside the slices. Thus $j_Z^*\dashv Rj_{Z*}$ on unbounded derived categories, and $Rj_{Z*}(Q I)=Q(j_{Z*}I)$ for every K-injective complex $I$ on the slice, where $Q$ denotes localization. There are natural derived identifications
$$j_U^*Rj_{U*}A\cong A,\quad j_U^*Rj_{V*}B\cong Rk_{U*}(k_V^*B),\quad j_U^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{U*}D,$$
$$j_V^*Rj_{V*}B\cong B,\quad j_V^*Rj_{U*}A\cong Rk_{V*}(k_U^*A),\quad j_V^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{V*}D,$$
and $Rj_{U*}Rk_{U*}\cong Rj_{W*}$, $Rj_{V*}Rk_{V*}\cong Rj_{W*}$. Here $A,B,D$ are arbitrary objects on the $U,V,W$ slices. The self-restriction identifications are the counits. For $A$ on $U$, define $r_A:Rj_{U*}A\to Rj_{W*}(k_U^*A)$ as the $j_W^*\dashv Rj_{W*}$ transpose of $k_U^*\epsilon_{U,A}$, using canonical iterated restriction; define $r_B$ likewise. The listed identifications carry $r_A|_U$ and $r_B|_V$ to the respective units for $k_U^*\dashv Rk_{U*}$ and $k_V^*\dashv Rk_{V*}$, carry $r_B|_U$ and $r_A|_V$ to the identity under the cross-identifications, and carry $r_A|_W,r_B|_W$ to identities under the self-restriction counits. All comparisons are induced on K-injective representatives by the sectionwise product identifications and preserve these adjunction maps.

proof.text: For any $Z=U,V,W$, apply [lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation] to the underlying set sheaf of a module $F$ on $\mathcal E/Z$. It gives a sheaf $C\mapsto F(C\times Z/Z)$. Give it addition and scalar action by those of $F(C\times Z/Z)$ and $R(C)\to R(C\times Z)$; restriction maps are semilinear, so this is an $R$-module sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $\alpha:j_Z^*M\to F$, its transpose has component $M(C)\to M(C\times Z)\xrightarrow{\alpha_{C\times Z/Z}}F(C\times Z/Z)$. Conversely restrict a map $M\to j_{Z*}F$ to $T\to Z$ and then restrict $F(T\times Z/Z)$ along the graph $T\to T\times Z$. Naturality of the two maps shows that these operations are inverse; both are linear, since the composite $R(T)\to R(T\times Z)\to R(T)$ is the identity. This gives the module adjunction $j_Z^*\dashv j_{Z*}$. Its unit is restriction along $C\times Z\to C$, and its counit is restriction along the graph. The same construction inside $\mathcal E/U$ and $\mathcal E/V$ gives $k_{U*},k_{V*}$ using fibre products over the slice base.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; module-linear specialization of the section formula and graph counit

proof.text: The categories $\mathcal E$, $\mathcal E/U$, $\mathcal E/V$, $\mathcal E/W$ are small sites: the objects and arrows of a slice are subsets of sets of pairs from $\mathcal E$. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to their restricted ring sheaves to obtain K-injective resolutions of every unbounded complex. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], every restriction in question is additive exact and has an additive exact left adjoint given by extension by zero. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] first to extension by zero $\dashv$ restriction, and then to restriction $\dashv$ the right adjoint constructed in step 1, proves that both restriction and direct image preserve K-injectives. These applications also take place within each slice.

Exact restriction induces its termwise triangulated functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to direct image on homotopy categories followed by localization: this functor is triangulated, since its additive termwise construction carries the cone matrix and shifts to the same cone matrix and shifts. The resolutions from step 2 give $Rj_{Z*}$ everywhere and $Rj_{Z*}(QI)\cong Q(j_{Z*}I)$ for K-injective $I$; likewise for $k_U,k_V$. In particular compositions can be computed without a second resolution, since the first direct image remains K-injective by step 2.

For any complex $M$ on $\mathcal E$ and K-injective $I$ on $\mathcal E/Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_Z)}(j_Z^*QM,QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R_Z)}(j_Z^*M,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R)}(M,j_{Z*}I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(QM,Qj_{Z*}I).$$
The last use of the K-injective Hom bijection is valid by step 2. Every derived object has such representatives by step 2, hence this is $j_Z^*\dashv Rj_{Z*}$. The homotopy adjunction in the cited statement sends a chain map to its ordinary transpose, so this bijection has exactly the ordinary counit at $QI$. For the unit choose $M$ K-injective as well; then $j_Z^*M$ is K-injective by step 2, so the unit is also represented by the ordinary unit. It is natural in derived morphisms because morphisms between K-injective representatives are homotopy classes and the displayed bijections are natural. The identical argument gives the two $k$ adjunctions.

proof.text: If $T\to U$ is an object of $\mathcal E/U$, the graph $T\to T\times U$ is inverse to the first projection: the two maps to $U$ coincide because $U$ is subterminal. Therefore the counit in step 1 identifies $(j_U^*j_{U*}F)(T/U)=F(T\times U/U)$ with $F(T/U)$. For $G$ on $\mathcal E/V$, the two expressions $(j_U^*j_{V*}G)(T/U)$ and $(k_{U*}k_V^*G)(T/U)$ are respectively $G(T\times V/V)$ and $G(T\times_U W/V)$. Their indexing objects are canonically isomorphic: $T\times_U(U\times V)\cong T\times V$. For $H$ on $\mathcal E/W$, $T\times W\cong T\times_U W$ because the map $T\to U$ is unique. This gives $j_U^*j_{W*}H\cong k_{U*}H$. Each isomorphism preserves the map from $R(T)$, and it commutes with restriction along $T'\to T$ by the product projections. Interchanging $U,V$ proves the other three underived comparisons.

source.place: Tags 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products, and 00Y2, lemma-restrict-back; direct product calculation from step 1

proof.text: For $H$ on $\mathcal E/W$, evaluate $j_{U*}k_{U*}H$ at $C$. Its value is $H((C\times U)\times_U W/W)=H(C\times W/W)$, the value of $j_{W*}H$. The scalar maps from $R(C)$ and all restriction maps agree under this product identification. Thus $j_{U*}k_{U*}\cong j_{W*}$. Interchanging $U,V$ gives $j_{V*}k_{V*}\cong j_{W*}$. Iterated restrictions also agree sectionwise, by the relocalization formula of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products, applied within a slice; product associativity

proof.text: Represent $A,B,D$ by K-injective complexes $I,J,L$ on $U,V,W$ respectively. In step 5 substitute $I,J,L$ degree by degree. The complex $k_V^*J$ is K-injective by step 2, so $k_{U*}k_V^*J$ computes $Rk_{U*}(k_V^*B)$, whereas $j_U^*j_{V*}J$ computes $j_U^*Rj_{V*}B$. The self and $W$ comparisons follow from the other two formulas in that step, and the $V$ formulas follow by interchange. In step 6, $k_{U*}L$ is K-injective, so the same formula computes the iterated derived direct image and gives $Rj_{U*}Rk_{U*}\cong Rj_{W*}$; similarly for $V$. These degreewise natural identifications are natural in the derived objects: by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] all their morphisms are represented by homotopy classes of chain maps, and additive functors and the product identifications respect chain homotopies. The self comparisons are the counits by step 4 and the graph calculation of step 5.

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, direct-image restriction calculation, made explicit for sites using steps 1–6

proof.text: For $A=QI$, the map $r_A$ is represented by the chain map $\rho_I:j_{U*}I\to j_{W*}k_U^*I$ whose component at $C$ is restriction $I(C\times U/U)\to I(C\times W/U)$. Indeed, its transpose under step 4 is restriction of this map to $W$ followed by the graph counit of $j_W$; at $T\to W$ this is the graph counit of $j_U$ restricted to $W$, namely $k_U^*\epsilon_{U,I}$. Both the source and target of $\rho_I$ are K-injective by step 2, so the Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies this chain calculation with the stated derived transpose, without a choice of a derived lift. For $B=QJ$ the same construction gives $\rho_J:j_{V*}J\to j_{W*}k_V^*J$.

source.place: Tag 08DG, lemma-glue, the obvious overlap map; explicit adjunction transpose calculation

proof.text: At $T\to U$, identify $I(T\times U/U)$ with $I(T/U)$ by the graph counit. The component of $\rho_I$ becomes $I(T/U)\to I(T\times_U W/U)$, exactly the unit of $k_U^*\dashv k_{U*}$ from step 1. On the other hand the component of $\rho_J$ at $T\to U$ is $J(T\times V/V)\to J(T\times W/V)$. The indexing arrow is an isomorphism, since $T\to U$ and $U$ is subterminal; under the cross-comparisons of step 5 both sides are the same module $J(T\times_U W/V)$ and this arrow is its identity. Interchanging $U,V$ yields respectively the unit for $r_B|_V$ and the identity for $r_A|_V$. At $T\to W$, all graph counits identify the indexing objects with $T$, so both $\rho_I|_W$ and $\rho_J|_W$ become identities. These computations are degreewise and natural in $T$, so after localization and the normalized adjunctions of step 4 they prove every asserted unit, counit and overlap-map compatibility.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses only the generic product formula for a slice direct image and its graph counit; the tower unit contains no site-theoretic proof of that formula.
Step 2 uses K-injective resolutions on arbitrary small ringed sites; this is a general homological tool, not a replacement of tower gluing.
Step 2 uses exact restriction and its exact extension-by-zero left adjoint on arbitrary ringed slices.
Step 2 uses the general exact-left-adjoint criterion, twice for each slice.
Step 3 uses general existence and computation of unbounded right derived functors on K-injectives.
Step 4 uses the Hom transpose of any additive adjunction on homotopy categories; the tower unit does not develop this generic tool.

The delivery is the first split of an item that Q106 created statement-only on 2026-10-21 when it re-split lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent (this item carries that proof's old steps 4-5). The item is unsplit on live and is not in any dropped list. The statement is unchanged and true: it is the direct-image part of Stacks 08DG (cohomology.tex lemma-glue, lines 11071-11124), generalised to subterminal objects of a small site with finite limits. No covering hypothesis is needed, and subterminality is used only in two places: the graph and the first projection are inverse on T×U for T→U, and T×W≅T×_U W. I checked all 9 steps by hand. Step 1: the module version of the 03CE/trf slice formula has R(T)→R(T×Z)→R(T) equal to the identity, its two transpose formulas are mutually inverse, and its counit is restriction along the graph. Step 2: the hypotheses of the 08BJ criterion hold, applied first to extension by zero ⊣ restriction and then to restriction ⊣ direct image. Step 3: 070K applies because a termwise additive functor carries cones and shifts to cones and shifts (014X, argued in the step). Step 4: the derived adjunction follows from the 070I bijections. Its counit is the ordinary counit at a K-injective I. Its unit is the ordinary one when M is K-injective, which the step correctly requires. Steps 5-6: the product identifications T×_U(U×V)≅T×V, T×W≅T×_U W and (C×U)×_U W≅C×W hold, and the scalar actions agree. Step 7: the derived comparisons hold on K-injective representatives, because k_V^*J and k_{U*}L are K-injective. Step 8: I recomputed the transpose of ρ_I; it is k_U^*ε, since T→T×W→T×U is the graph. Step 9: on U the map is the unit, ρ_J is the identity under the cross identifications, and on W both maps are identities by the triangle identity. Small cases tested: U=V=1, U=V, disjoint opens, U initial, a non-covering pair, the zero ring. No duplicate exists. The nearest nodes are subterminal-module-local-calculus (the extension-by-zero side, with a covering hypothesis), the scheme-only lem-pc Mayer-Vietoris and open-image nodes, and kinjective-restrict-localized (a single clause). I accept all six declared tool_uses as generic foundations; no SGA is cited. Batch 5: I accept the citation of lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation. It is the generic Stacks 03CE/00Y2 slice-site lemma. Its 121-node closure contains only generic site, sheaf and module foundations and the definition def-trf-geometric-morphism, with no trace-formula, Poincaré or batch-4 node. It is not a statement or proof step of either assumption, and Q08 passed it on 2026-10-17.
